The '''Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action''' ('''JCPOA'''; {{lang-fa|برنامه جامع اقدام مشترک |barnāme jāme‘ eqdām moshtarak}}, [[acronym]]: {{lang|fa|برجام}} '''BARJAM'''<ref>{{IPA-fa|bæɾˈdʒɒːm|pron}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.tehrantimes.com/index_View.asp?code=248149 |title=Zarif: We've never claimed nuclear deal only favors Iran |work=[[Tehran Times]] |date=22 July 2015}}</ref>), known commonly as the '''Iran deal''' or '''Iran nuclear deal''', is an international agreement on the [[nuclear program of Iran]] reached in [[Vienna]] on 14 July 2015 between [[Iran]], the [[P5+1]] (the five [[permanent members of the United Nations Security Council]]—[[China]], [[France]], [[Russia]], [[United Kingdom]], [[United States]]—plus [[Germany]]),{{efn|The P5+1 are also sometimes referred to as the "E3+3" (for the "[[EU three]]" countries (France, the UK, and Germany) plus the three non-EU countries (the U.S., Russia, and China)). The terms are interchangeable. This article uses the "P5+1" phrase.<ref>Joshua Keating, [https://foreignpolicy.com/2009/09/30/you-say-p51-i-say-e33/ "You say P5+1, I say E3+3"], ''Foreign Policy'' (30 September 2009).</ref><ref>Jeffrey Lewis, [http://lewis.armscontrolwonk.com/archive/7773/e3eu3-or-p51 "E3/EU+3 or P5+1"], ''Arms Control Wonk'' (13 July 2015).</ref>}} and the [[European Union]].

Formal negotiations toward the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action on Iran's nuclear program began with the adoption of the [[Joint Plan of Action]], an interim agreement signed between Iran and the P5+1 countries in November 2013. For the next twenty months, Iran and the P5+1 countries engaged in negotiations, and in April 2015 agreed on an [[Iran nuclear deal framework]] for the final agreement and in July 2015, Iran and the P5+1 agreed on the plan.

Under the agreement, Iran agreed to eliminate its stockpile of medium-[[enriched uranium]], cut its stockpile of low-enriched uranium by 98%, and reduce by about two-thirds the number of its [[gas centrifuge]]s for 13 years. For the next 15 years, Iran will only enrich uranium up to 3.67%. Iran also agreed not to build any new [[pressurized heavy-water reactor|heavy-water facilities]] for the same period of time. Uranium-enrichment activities will be limited to a single facility using first-generation centrifuges for 10 years. Other facilities will be converted to avoid [[Nuclear proliferation|proliferation]] risks. To monitor and verify Iran's compliance with the agreement, the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA) will have regular access to all Iranian nuclear facilities. The agreement provides that in return for verifiably abiding by its commitments, Iran will receive relief from U.S., European Union, and [[United Nations Security Council]] nuclear-related economic [[Sanctions against Iran|sanctions]].

On 13 October 2017, U.S. President Donald Trump announced that the United States would not make the certification provided for under [[Iran Nuclear Agreement Review Act of 2015|U.S. domestic law]], but stopped short of terminating the deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://heavy.com/news/2017/10/trump-iran-live-stream-strategy-nuclear-deal/|title=LIVE STREAM: President Trump Announces Iran Nuclear Deal Strategy|first=Chris|last=Bucher|date=13 October 2017|publisher=|accessdate=6 January 2018}}</ref>
